title: Lehi Addresses Jacob
summary: Lehi speaks to Jacob about his childhood afflictions and the greatness of God.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi addresses Jacob as his first-born, born during Lehi’s tribulation in the wilderness.
Jacob suffered afflictions and much sorrow in childhood because of his brethren’s rudeness.
Lehi says Jacob knows the greatness of God and that God shall consecrate Jacob’s afflictions for his gain.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi and Jacob are together while Lehi addresses him.
unspecified_visual_details: Their posture, clothing, ages, and precise surroundings.

spoken_dialogue.text: And now, Jacob, I speak unto you:
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lehi

spoken_dialogue.text: Nevertheless, Jacob, my first-born in the wilderness, thou knowest the greatness of God; and he shall consecrate thine afflictions for thy gain.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lehi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Lehi’s references to Jacob’s past afflictions are counsel, not a separate event shown in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the brothers mistreating Jacob in this moment.

title: Lehi’s Words to Jacob
summary: Lehi speaks to Jacob about his blessing, future with Nephi, service to God, redemption, and what he has beheld.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi says Jacob’s soul shall be blessed, he shall dwell safely with Nephi, and his days shall be spent in the service of God.
Lehi says Jacob is redeemed through the righteousness of his Redeemer, and that Jacob has beheld that the Redeemer comes in the fulness of time to bring salvation to men.
Lehi says Jacob beheld the Redeemer’s glory in his youth and is blessed like those to whom the Redeemer shall minister in the flesh.
Lehi says the Spirit is the same yesterday, today, and forever, the way is prepared from the fall of man, and salvation is free.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi is addressing Jacob; the Redeemer and the events referred to are not shown as occurring in the present moment.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance and age of Lehi and Jacob, their gestures, clothing, and exact surroundings.

narration.text: thou shalt dwell safely with thy brother, Nephi;
I know that thou art redeemed, because of the righteousness of thy Redeemer;
thou hast beheld in thy youth his glory;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Redeemer’s coming and Jacob’s earlier beholding of his glory are mentioned, not narrated as present events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Redeemer or a vision; no appearance is described in these verses.

title: Law and Redemption
summary: The passage teaches that men know good from evil, that the law is given, and that redemption comes through the Holy Messiah, who offers himself as a sacrifice for sin for those with a broken heart and a contrite spirit.

explicit_facts.text: Men are instructed sufficiently that they know good from evil, and the law is given unto men.
By the law no flesh is justified; by the temporal law men were cut off, and by the spiritual law they perish from that which is good and become miserable forever.
Redemption comes in and through the Holy Messiah, who is full of grace and truth.
The Holy Messiah offers himself as a sacrifice for sin to answer the ends of the law for those with a broken heart and a contrite spirit; unto none else can the ends of the law be answered.

unspecified_visual_details: Any setting, figures, or visual symbolism.

narration.text: And men are instructed sufficiently that they know good from evil. And the law is given unto men.
And by the law no flesh is justified;
Wherefore, redemption cometh in and through the Holy Messiah; for he is full of grace and truth.
Behold, he offereth himself a sacrifice for sin, to answer the ends of the law,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The sacrifice and redemption are taught, not narrated as present events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the sacrifice or invent an appearance for the Holy Messiah; neither is narrated here.

title: The Messiah and Resurrection
summary: The verses teach that the Holy Messiah lays down his life and takes it again by the power of the Spirit, bringing about the resurrection of the dead. He is the first to rise, makes intercession for all the children of men, and those who believe in him shall be saved.

explicit_facts.text: The Holy Messiah lays down his life according to the flesh and takes it again by the power of the Spirit to bring about the resurrection of the dead; he is the first that should rise.
He shall make intercession for all the children of men, and those who believe in him shall be saved.

reasonable_visual_inferences: These statements are teachings; the verses do not narrate the Messiah's death or resurrection as events happening in the scene.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker and setting are not specified.
The Messiah's appearance is not described.

title: Judgment and Opposition
summary: Lehi teaches about judgment, the law’s punishment and happiness, and opposition in all things.
characters: First-born in the wilderness (addressed; identity unspecified by these verses)

explicit_facts.text: All men come unto God and stand in his presence to be judged according to the truth and holiness in him.
The law's affixed punishment is in opposition to its affixed happiness, to answer the ends of the atonement.
Lehi says opposition in all things is necessary for righteousness and wickedness, holiness and misery, and good and bad.
Lehi addresses “my first-born in the wilderness.”

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi is teaching; the statements about judgment and opposition are teachings, not a narrated visible judgment event.
unspecified_visual_details: The teaching location and the appearance of Lehi and the person addressed.
Any visual representation of judgment, punishment, happiness, or opposition.

narration.text: For it must needs be, that there is an opposition in all things.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses identify the addressee only as Lehi’s first-born in the wilderness; do not supply a personal name.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict God or a judgment assembly as a present scene.
Do not literalize the teachings or invent visual forms for abstract conditions.

title: Creation and Purpose
summary: Lehi speaks to his sons about the consequences of denying law, sin, righteousness, and God, and affirms that God created all things.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi argues that if creation had been for nothing, it would have had no purpose, and that this would destroy the wisdom, eternal purposes, power, mercy, and justice of God.
Lehi teaches that if there is no law, there is no sin; if there is no sin, there is no righteousness; and without righteousness there is no happiness, punishment, or misery.
Lehi says that if these things are not, there is no God, and without God there could have been no creation of things; all things would have vanished away.
Lehi says God created all things, including the heavens and the earth and all things in them.
Lehi addresses his sons and says he speaks for their profit and learning.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi is teaching his sons; the verses do not narrate creation or the vanishing of things as present events.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance, number, and positions of Lehi’s sons.

narration.text: Wherefore, it must needs have been created for a thing of naught;
And now, my sons, I speak unto you these things for your profit and learning;
for there is a God, and he hath created all things,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The conditional claims and the reference to vanishing are part of Lehi’s argument, not narrated visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict creation or the disappearance of the earth as occurring in this scene.
Do not depict God or assign visual features to him.

title: Opposition and Agency
summary: The verses describe opposition between the forbidden fruit and the tree of life, and state that the Lord God gave man the ability to act for himself, though he could not act for himself unless enticed by one or the other.

explicit_facts.text: After creating the first parents, the beasts of the field, the fowls of the air, and all created things, there was opposition: the forbidden fruit in opposition to the tree of life; one was sweet and the other bitter.
The Lord God gave man that he should act for himself; man could not act for himself unless enticed by one or the other.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic contrast between fruit and the tree of life may illustrate the stated opposition, without depicting a choice or eating.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether any person or setting is shown; the appearance and placement of the fruit and tree; how the contrast between sweet and bitter is represented.

narration.text: it must needs be that there was an opposition;
the forbidden fruit in opposition to the tree of life;
the one being sweet and the other bitter.
the Lord God gave unto man that he should act for himself.
man could not act for himself save it should be that he was enticed by the one or the other.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses teach about opposition and the ability to act for oneself.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray the teaching as a newly occurring event or invent the appearance of the Lord God, the first parents, or any location.

title: Lehi’s Account of the Fall and the Words to Eve
summary: Lehi supposes, based on what he has read, that an angel of God fell from heaven and became a devil. Lehi says the devil sought the misery of all mankind and spoke to Eve, urging her to partake of the forbidden fruit.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi says he supposes, according to what he has read, that an angel of God had fallen from heaven and become a devil.
Lehi says the devil sought the misery of all mankind and spoke to Eve, urging her to partake of the forbidden fruit and saying she would not die but would be as God, knowing good and evil.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi is the source of the account; the reported fall and words to Eve are not necessarily events occurring in the scene.
unspecified_visual_details: Lehi’s appearance, posture, and setting; the appearances and setting of the angel, devil, serpent, and Eve.

narration.text: And I, Lehi, according to the things which I have read, must needs suppose that an angel of God, according to that which is written, had fallen from heaven;
Partake of the forbidden fruit, and ye shall not die, but ye shall be as God, knowing good and evil.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Lehi frames the account of the angel’s fall as his supposition based on what he has read.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the reported fall or words to Eve as witnessed present events.
Do not invent physical appearances or settings for figures not described in these verses.

title: Adam and Eve Leave Eden
summary: After Adam and Eve partook of the forbidden fruit, they were driven out of the garden of Eden to till the earth. They brought forth children, even the family of all the earth.

explicit_facts.text: After Adam and Eve partook of the forbidden fruit, they were driven out of the garden of Eden to till the earth.
Adam and Eve brought forth children; yea, even the family of all the earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The verses report the departure and the bringing forth of children; no particular moment or staging is specified.
unspecified_visual_details: Their appearance, the garden's appearance, how they were driven out, the children’s number and appearance, and the setting of the report are not specified.

narration.text: they were driven out of the garden of Eden, to till the earth.
And they have brought forth children; yea, even the family of all the earth.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses report events; no speaker or present-time setting is identified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a speaker, dialogue, appearance, expulsion mechanism, or details about the children.

title: Probation and Repentance
summary: The days of the children of men were prolonged so that they might repent while in the flesh. Their state became a state of probation, and their time was lengthened. God commanded all men to repent and showed all men that they were lost because of their parents’ transgression.

explicit_facts.text: The days of the children of men were prolonged according to the will of God, so that they might repent while in the flesh.
Their state became a state of probation, and their time was lengthened according to the commandments the Lord God gave to the children of men.
God gave commandment that all men must repent.
God showed all men that they were lost because of the transgression of their parents.

reasonable_visual_inferences: This is teaching about humankind's condition and responsibility, not a narrated visible event.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker, audience, setting, and any visual representation of probation, repentance, or God's command are not specified.

narration.text: For he gave commandment that all men must repent;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage does not narrate a particular person or moment of repentance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Lehi or Jacob as present; this verse does not identify a speaker or audience.
Do not depict a visible divine command or a specific act of repentance.

title: What If Adam Had Not Fallen
summary: The verses describe what would have been if Adam had not transgressed: he would not have fallen and would have remained in the garden of Eden. All created things would have remained in their created state forever, without end. They would have had no children and would have remained innocent, without joy because they knew no misery, and doing no good because they knew no sin.

explicit_facts.text: If Adam had not transgressed, he would not have fallen and would have remained in the garden of Eden.
All things which were created would have remained in the same state in which they were after they were created, forever, and without end.
They would have had no children and would have remained in a state of innocence, having no joy because they knew no misery, and doing no good because they knew no sin.

reasonable_visual_inferences: These verses present hypothetical outcomes rather than a narrated event; avoid staging them as a present-time scene.
unspecified_visual_details: No visual setting or figures are specified.

narration.text: And now, behold, if Adam had not transgressed he would not have fallen,
And they would have had no children;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses state a counterfactual teaching.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray a hypothetical alternate Eden or stage Adam and others as present in an event.

title: Wisdom, the Fall, and Joy
summary: The verses state that all things have been done in wisdom, and that Adam fell so men might be and men might have joy.

explicit_facts.text: All things have been done in the wisdom of him who knoweth all things.
Adam fell that men might be, and men are, that they might have joy.

unspecified_visual_details: Whether a speaker or listeners are present; any appearance, setting, posture, or visual symbolism.

narration.text: But behold, all things have been done in the wisdom of him who knoweth all things.
Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses state teachings; they do not narrate Adam's fall as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Adam's fall as a present event or invent a speaker, listener, or visible divine figure.

title: Freedom Through the Messiah
summary: Lehi teaches that the Messiah comes in the fulness of time to redeem the children of men from the fall, and that people are free to choose liberty and eternal life or captivity and death.

explicit_facts.text: The Messiah comes in the fulness of time to redeem the children of men from the fall.
Those redeemed from the fall become free forever, knowing good from evil, to act for themselves rather than be acted upon, except by the punishment of the law at the great and last day.
People are free according to the flesh, and all things expedient unto man are given them.
People may choose liberty and eternal life through the great Mediator of all men, or captivity and death according to the captivity and power of the devil.
The devil seeks that all men might be miserable like unto himself.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi may be shown teaching; the supplied verses do not specify the location or listeners.
unspecified_visual_details: Lehi's appearance, the location and audience, and any visual symbols for freedom or captivity.

or to choose captivity and death,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The alternatives are presented as teaching, not as separate literal events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Messiah, the devil, or the great and last day as physically present; their appearances are not described in these verses.

title: Lehi’s Final Counsel
summary: Lehi counsels his sons to look to the Mediator and choose eternal life, warns against eternal death, and says he has chosen the good part and seeks their everlasting welfare.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi tells his sons to look to the great Mediator, heed his commandments, be faithful to his words, and choose eternal life according to the will of the Holy Spirit.
Lehi tells his sons not to choose eternal death according to the will of the flesh and the evil therein, which gives the spirit of the devil power to captivate and bring them down to hell.
Lehi says he has spoken these words to his sons in the last days of his probation, has chosen the good part according to the prophet’s words, and seeks their everlasting welfare.

unspecified_visual_details: The setting, Lehi’s and his sons’ appearances, and which sons are present.
